_doc: RATE-1022: per-portal rate-limit adapters (vera/rate_limit.py). rate_per_s/burst = token bucket; max_concurrency = in-flight cap; daily_cap = requests SENT per UTC day (throttled ones included; skips never sent are not counted). Throttles (throttle_statuses or caller-flagged anti-bot pages) halve the rate (AIMD) and set a cooldown: Retry-After when sent (clamped to retry_after_max_s), else base_cooldown_s doubling per consecutive throttle up to max_cooldown_s, plus upward-only jitter. The breaker opens after breaker_failures consecutive throttles/failures for breaker_open_s (doubling per failed half-open probe, up to breaker_open_max_s). acquire() waits at most min(max_wait_s, caller deadline - min_call_s), otherwise it skips at once. 429/cooldown tries never count as attempts; they are always counted as requests. No email is sent anywhere: contact_param is used only if VERA_CONTACT_EMAIL is set (unset by default).
_calibration_note: UNCALIBRATED against live traffic. Sources were read 2026-10-21 by the research-reader agent through WebFetch (a summarizing fetch, not raw page text: every quote is a paraphrase-level check). Where a portal documents a ceiling, rate_per_s is set at or BELOW it (planner prior chosen for a shared Render egress IP, where other tenants spend the same per-IP allowance); where nothing is documented the value is a planner prior, flagged 'prior'. The AIMD, breaker and cooldown defaults are planner priors (no live spread measured). What would change them: the per-portal 'ratelimit' log line and /health/dar aggregates over a week of live inline runs (429 share, skip share, time in cooldown, and inline yield); raise a rate only up to its documented ceiling.

defaults._max_wait_stream_note: RETRIEVAL-1109 A2 / owner H-T (OD-1109-RETRIEVAL, approved 2026-11-09 as relayed by the coordinator). STREAMED path only (vera.rate_limit.stream_wait_scope, set by vera.inline_acquire._run when stream_ctx is active): a call that would need a token or concurrency wait longer than max_wait_s waits up to this many seconds instead of being skipped as 'pacing'. Rates are unchanged: the wait is the pacing (tokens reserved in order, max_concurrency kept), and cooldown, breaker and daily-cap skips stay immediate. Switch: set equal to max_wait_s (2.0) or delete the key for the old skip behaviour. Calibration note for 30: the slowest paced acquisition portal hit inline is Europe PMC at rate_per_s 0.1 with robots Crawl-delay 10 (10 s per request; a full text is about 3 requests, NOANSWER-ROOT-1109 e3), so a queued caller can need up to 2-3 slots (20-30 s); 30 covers that and stays far below the 300 s stream stall rule. Not measured on live waits; what would change it: the per-request 'autoacq ratelimit_request' waited_ms and skip lines over live streamed asks. Portals slower than 1 per 30 s (plos 1/30 s, openaire 1/60 s) still skip a second call within one interval.
defaults._note: Planner priors. max_wait_s 2 keeps any in-request wait far below the 45 s inline deadline (config/auto_acquire.json inline.deadline_s); min_call_s 1 is the least time left for a call to be worth sending.

openalex._with_key_1110_note: SEARCHCAPS-1110 (owner OD-1110-SEARCHCAPS, 2026-11-10, OpenAlex 'Free key + raise cap'): when the env var OPENALEX_API_KEY is set (NAME only; the value is loaded at runtime, sent as the api_key query parameter per the OpenAlex docs, redacted from errors and never logged) the OpenAlex search cap is 1000/day (search_daily_cap, read by OpenAlexProvider; half of it reserved for visitors by origin.visitor_reserve_frac) and pacing is rate 4/s with burst 1, so at most 5 requests in any 1 s window (owner: pace <= 5 requests/second; the documented keyed limit is higher). The former with_key prior (2/s, burst 4) is superseded. Without the key nothing changes: the cap stays search.openalex.daily_search_budget 90 (config/vera_eval_run.json) and the rate 1/s. Owner-decided values, not calibrated thresholds; what would change them: OpenAlex 429s or X-RateLimit-Remaining with the key, and the daily spend by origin.
openalex._searchcaps_1110_note: OD-1110-SEARCHCAPS (owner 2026-11-10): origin.visitor_reserve_frac 0.5 = owner 'reserve half for visitors': a request marked origin=seed stops at floor(cap x 0.5) of the OpenAlex search cap (45 of the keyless 90); visitors may use the whole cap. Owner-decided value, not a calibrated threshold; what would change it: the per-day OpenAlex spend split by origin.

groq._enabled_note: INT-1022-B (orchestrator disposition 2026-10-22): disabled until calibrated against Groq headers live. /ask makes about 3 Groq calls within a few seconds, which the uncalibrated prior (0.5/s, burst 2, max_wait 1 s) could skip. With enabled=false the OpenAI-SDK clients get no rate-limit transport at all (vera.rate_limit.openai_http_client returns None), so LLM calls behave exactly as at 76ceb2a. Calibrate from live x-ratelimit-* headers and 429 counts, then set true.
